contributes.instructions: The css-author plugin judges every landing with two BLOCKING gates after the format gate: the static lint (facts from the JSON alone — a length with no unit, a restated initial value, a container query no ancestor can answer, a font face nothing names) and the necessity lint (each declaration removed in the rendered page and restored; one that changes no element's geometry or computed style at the viewport's width nor at a sweep of other widths is dead). Treat their findings as the Core tools section says. A viewport is authored as a draft the user watches take shape: draft_open is the FIRST call of the task — the frame, the title and the html › body skeleton with its page background (never a page without one), sent before knowledge_bundle, before any reading, before planning — then knowledge_bundle {query: <the task in a few words>} ONCE (it returns the format rules with the example nearest the task), then one visual group per draft_append as each is written — a rule the group shares goes in first, ahead of its elements — then draft_finalize, which alone lands it. The layout procedures (which formatting context, whether a declaration is needed at all, where in the cascade it goes) are this plugin's: read them once per task with knowledge_read {path: "mrbavio.css-author/procedures.md"} (or the `procedures` resource) and judge every declaration by them. The author → land → fix workflow is Daydream's own dream-author prompt: start every document task from it.
